<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="חשון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915165_theRebbe_61" batchId="meluket-_D7_97_D7_A9_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915165_theRebbe_61__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section questions why the name Elokim is used in Yitzchak's blessing to Yaakov, and why the blessing includes Torah study which was already destined for Israel.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Now, it must be understood why it says "Elokim besides You,"</t>
    <t s="1">specifically the name Elokim.</t>
    <t s="2">And likewise, it must be understood in our portion,</t>
    <t s="3">the verse "And may Elokim give you of the dew of the heavens and of the fatness of the earth and abundance of grain and wine,"</t>
    <t s="4">and this is questioned in many places, and also in the continuation of the year 5666,</t>
    <t s="5">why it says Elokim,</t>
    <t s="6">for seemingly it should have said the name Havayah,</t>
    <t s="7">since the main aspect of blessings is specifically from the name Havayah,</t>
    <t s="8">and especially Yitzchak's blessings, which are most exalted blessings,</t>
    <t s="9">as explained in the Siddur at the end of Shaar HaTekios.</t>
    <t s="10">Also, it is not understood, as it is brought in Midrash Rabbah,</t>
    <t s="11">"dew of the heavens" refers to Scripture, "fatness of the earth" refers to Mishnah, "grain" refers to Talmud, etc.,</t>
    <t s="12">and it must be understood what is the concept of blessing him with Torah,</t>
    <t s="13">for seemingly a blessing for this is not applicable.</t>
    <t s="14">For the Torah was to be given to Israel anyway at the giving of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="15">since the primary intention in the creation of the worlds was for the sake of the Torah, as our sages said,</t>
    <t s="16">on the verse "In the beginning He created," etc.,</t>
    <t s="17">"for the sake of Israel who are called 'first,'" etc., "and for the sake of the Torah which is called 'first,'" etc.,</t>
    <t s="18">that the Torah was established in the nature of creation,</t>
    <t s="19">and in a manner of a condition, that when the condition is nullified, the thing is nullified,</t>
    <t s="20">and as it is brought in the Gemara,</t>
    <t s="21">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="22">"And there was evening... the sixth day,"</t>
    <t s="23">"The Holy One, blessed be He, made a condition with the works of creation: if Israel fulfills My Torah, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="24">and this is as it is written,</t>
    <t s="25">"From the heavens... the earth feared and was still," etc.,</t>
    <t s="26">"at first it feared, and at the end it was still,"</t>
    <t s="27">and if so, the giving of the Torah was a necessary thing, so how can a blessing apply to this?</t>
    <t s="28">Also, it must be said,</t>
    <t s="29">that whichever way you look at it,</t>
    <t s="30">if the intention of the blessing was for the study of Torah as it was before the giving of the Torah, surely no blessing was needed for this,</t>
    <t s="31">for there was already Torah study by the Patriarchs,</t>
    <t s="32">and as our sages said,</t>
    <t s="33">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="34">"And Avraham was old,"</t>
    <t s="35">"Avraham our Patriarch was old and sat in the study hall... Yaakov our Patriarch was old and sat in the study hall."</t>
    <t s="36">And also it cannot be said that the intention is for the Torah as it is after the giving of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="37">for the Torah of the Patriarchs</t>
    <t s="38">(which includes Yaakov as well)</t>
    <t s="39">was like a fragrance compared to the Torah after the giving of the Torah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section considers the possibility that Yitzchak's blessing of Torah was intended for Esav, but questions how it applies to Yaakov who actually received it.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And seemingly it could be explained,</t>
    <t s="1">that this was according to Yitzchak's initial thought,</t>
    <t s="2">when he sought to bless Esav,</t>
    <t s="3">and therefore he blessed him with Torah, thinking that through this he would be refined,</t>
    <t s="4">and for Esav a blessing for this is applicable,</t>
    <t s="5">because the Torah is only obligatory for Israel.</t>
    <t s="6">But nevertheless, it is not understood,</t>
    <t s="7">for in actuality the blessings were given to Yaakov,</t>
    <t s="8">and as it is written,</t>
    <t s="9">"Now he has taken my blessing,"</t>
    <t s="10">and they make of the blessings a great matter, etc.,</t>
    <t s="11">and according to this, it is not understood what is the concept of the blessing to Yaakov regarding Torah, etc.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that Yitzchak's blessing was for toil in Torah, which draws from a level above the Torah itself, enabling the refinement of even the harshest impurities.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">But the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="1">that the Torah as it was given at the giving of the Torah is the aspect of the Torah as it is in its own essence,</t>
    <t s="2">but Yitzchak's blessing was for the matter of toil in Torah,</t>
    <t s="3">about which it is said,</t>
    <t s="4">"He will do for those who wait for Him,"</t>
    <t s="5">and it is brought in the Zohar,</t>
    <t s="6">"those who press into the word of wisdom,"</t>
    <t s="7">that through this they reach a level above the aspect of the Torah as it is in its own essence,</t>
    <t s="8">for the Torah in its own essence is the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="9">and higher than that is the aspect of the Concealed Wisdom,</t>
    <t s="10">and through toil they reach the aspect of Eden, etc., about which it is said "No eye has seen," etc., as above,</t>
    <t s="11">which is entirely above the aspect of wisdom.</t>
    <t s="12">Based on this, Yitzchak's initial thought that he wanted to bless Esav so that he would be refined is also understood,</t>
    <t s="13">for seemingly how does this fit with the actual outcome</t>
    <t s="14">(and the Patriarchs are the Merkavah),</t>
    <t s="15">but rather, through the blessings that he blessed Yaakov regarding toil in Torah,</t>
    <t s="16">through this the power was given to refine Esav,</t>
    <t s="17">for since through toil they draw from the aspect of Eden,</t>
    <t s="18">therefore he can refine not only the kelipah of nogah but also the sparks within the three completely impure kelipot, etc.</t>
    <t s="19">And as explained elsewhere,</t>
    <t s="20">regarding "And Yaakov sent... 'I have sojourned with Lavan,'"</t>
    <t s="21">that then he completed the refinement with Lavan and went to refine Esav,</t>
    <t s="22">for Yaakov in his own essence was already prepared for this then,</t>
    <t s="23">and from Yaakov's side the refinement was then completed, etc.,</t>
    <t s="24">and this is through the blessings regarding toil in Torah.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
